L01.why: Active 'has preserved' needs an object and a singular subject, the narrowest fit of the four; all remain possible.

L02.why: Bare 'did' as an auxiliary/main verb fits fewer frames than the perfect auxiliaries, but any could fit.

L03.why: Plural active 'seal' needs a plural agent subject and an object; every option is grammatical in some sentence.

L04.why: A pair of colons cannot bracket an appositive and a colon cannot sit directly before 'and' in a list, so C fails in any sentence.

L05.why: Future perfect is the rarest fit, but a forward-looking sentence could require it.

L06.why: Plural past passive needs a plural subject in a past frame; each option fits some sentence.

L07.why: No punctuation would fuse clauses if 'Any' starts a new one, but 'oxygen any longer' could be a single clause.

L08.why: Past perfect needs an earlier-past anchor; all four tenses are possible.

L09.why: Past perfect passive needs a past anchor; each option has a plausible frame.

L10.why: A dash opening and a comma closing an appositive is mismatched, though a dash could introduce a list of names.

L11.why: Singular present perfect needs a singular subject; each option fits some sentence.

L12.why: Plural active needs a plural agent and an object; all four are grammatical in some frame.

L13.why: Active past perfect needs an object and an earlier-past anchor; all remain possible.

L14.why: No punctuation may fuse clauses, but 'magnification deep' could be a single phrase; none is certain.

L15.why: Past perfect needs an earlier-past anchor; finite and participial forms each fit some frame.

L16.why: Perfect participle is the narrowest fit; finite and participial forms each fit some sentence.
